citations.narrative:
During inspection, no acquisition or disposition forms were available for review and an acquisition form dated 30
September 2026 was provided the day after the inspection concluded. This form is incomplete and missing required
elements such as the date of acquisition, name and address from whom the animals were obtained and the species of
animals. Failure to maintain complete acquisition and disposition records interferes with the ability to accurately identify
animals and trace their movement. The licensee shall make, keep, and maintain records that fully and correctly disclose
information concerning regulated animals purchased, born, hatched or otherwise acquired, as well as animals
transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise disposed.
Correct by 19 October 2026.

The facility did not have an active contingency plan at time of inspection and provided a contingency plan dated 30
September 2026, the day after the inspection concluded. Failure to develop a complete contingency plan may result in
poor response to emergencies that can negatively affect animal welfare. Each exhibitor must develop, document and
follow an appropriate plan to provide for the humane handling, treatment, transportation, housing, and care of their
animals in the event of an emergency or disaster. Corrected on 30 September 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
